evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, 元 entry
evidence.field: 形義通解; dated graph uses and citations
evidence.text: The account describes early oracle-bone and bronze forms as a human figure with a round point or square marking the head; that mark could be reduced to a horizontal stroke, sometimes with an added short decorative stroke. It reports oracle-bone 元卜 in Heji 23390 as ‘first divination,’ and bronze uses including 元年 on 師酉簋, ‘first year,’ and 元德 on 番生簋蓋, ‘great virtue.’ It says the cited inscriptional examples do not use 元 for ‘head,’ though transmitted Zuo zhuan and Mengzi passages do. The page also reports a proposal that 元 and 兀 split from one graph and an alternative reading of the upper strokes as 上 above 人; it challenges the latter against the dot-marked early form. These are the page’s reported analyses, not independent inspection of the cited artifacts.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：古文字字形表, 元

limitations.text: This is a modern redraw of a seal-script form, not a photograph or facsimile of an ancient artifact; it cannot by itself establish the early graph’s specific strokes or semantic interpretation.
